solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put wine in case without top, being careful

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so one piece goes within the other
a word missing its top has lost its first letter, as a down-written word loses its head

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone is careful while packing wine into a crate that has no lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a box but is grammatical: the dative is one of the noun cases in Latin and German. 'Put' is the instruction to place the wine inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An attentive person is paying close heed, which is a synonym for acting carefully.

clue.text: Exhausted old dog nothing less reared to guard very traditional club

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up means reading from bottom to top
a guard stands around what it protects, so the outer letters enclose the inner
less means minus, so the stated letter is taken away from the dog

parts.note: all in means worn out
standard abbreviation for old
the tosa is a Japanese fighting dog breed
nothing is zero, the letter O
standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A weary old hound is pictured somehow tied to a club with long traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: TOSA loses an O to give TSA; ALL IN + O + TSA reversed gives ASTONILLA, which wraps round V. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club founded in 1874.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is one of England's oldest football clubs, a founder member of the Football League.

clue.text: Company it's claimed with time in part of autumn for dance

parts.note: the saying claims two's company, three's a crowd

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the letter for time sits within the month

parts.note: September, abbreviated, is part of autumn
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dance is held with company at some point in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's claimed' refers to the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd'. Sep is the calendar abbreviation for September.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom and country dance named for its basic step pattern.

clue.text: Harry Truman agonised internally

indicators.note: internally points to letters inside the phrase rather than to its meaning

parts.note: sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A US president is tormented by inner anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is not Truman's first name here but a verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass them persistently, a synonym of the verb to nag.

clue.text: Friend not delayed rounding up volunteers

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so one phrase encloses the other

parts.note: arriving in time is not being late

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A friend who is punctual helps gather volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate is a close friend, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Comedienne providing teatime treat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: surname of the British stand-up Jenny ...
second meaning: a cream-filled choux pastry

explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Eclair is a British comedian and writer; her stage surname is also the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry with cream and chocolate, eaten as a cake at tea.

clue.text: Model entertaining small legal team

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to model is to pose
standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A model is hosting a little group of lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal team' suggests lawyers, but it is the sheriff's band of deputised citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a body of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law, hence a team acting legally.

clue.text: Extremely productive past master fantastically showing off what's foremost in tennis?

definitions.text: Extremely productive past master fantastically showing off what's foremost in tennis?

indicators.note: fantastically signals the letters being rearranged in an extraordinary way
off means removed, so the named letter is taken away
extremely points to the two extreme letters, first and last, of the next word

parts.note: first and last letters
taken as written
the foremost letter

explanation.surface: A prolific, brilliant past master shows off the very best of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: One T of the two in the fodder is removed before the remaining nine letters are shuffled; the whole clue then describes the player.
explanation.definitionFit: Pete Sampras, winner of fourteen Grand Slam singles titles, is an acknowledged past master of tennis.

clue.text: Exotic gastronome lacking no bit of meat for safekeeping

indicators.note: exotic means strange and unusual, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order
lacking means without, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first bit

explanation.surface: An adventurous foodie skips meat, keeping it aside safely.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N, O and M out of GASTRONOME, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the keeping of things in a place for later, a synonym for safekeeping.

clue.text: Greek character interrupted by new source of fumes?

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Greek man is interrupted by something new that sets him fuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person; it is a letter. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active Sicilian volcano, which belches smoke and gas, an example of a fume source.

clue.text: Fancy hotel found in unfortunate town principally

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

parts.note: tough luck is bad fortune
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the principal letter

explanation.surface: A posh hotel sits in a down-on-its-luck town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the hotel; here it is a noun meaning an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or idea that occurs to one, a sense close to a thought.

clue.text: Eastern European called fluffy hair a disappointment

indicators.note: called means spoken out, so the word counts for how it is said

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
down is soft fine hair or feathers

explanation.surface: A Latvian dismissed someone's fluffy hairstyle as a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax or disappointment, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Dapper attorney in US city

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: New York
Att. is an abbreviation for attorney

explanation.surface: A well-dressed lawyer works in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neat in dress, a close synonym of dapper.

clue.text: Directory left by humble attendant inside certainly

indicators.note: inside means the earlier pieces sit within the word that follows

parts.note: yes is an affirmation, as is certainly
standard abbreviation for left
low means lowly, humble
a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: A directory of staff lists a humble attendant beside the departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left by' reads like abandonment, but it simply places the letter for left beside the next piece; 'certainly' then wraps all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yellow Pages is a telephone directory of businesses, printed on yellow paper.

clue.text: Chief support provided by mother during visit

parts.note: familiar word for mother
in means during, as in 'in the summer'
a stay is a visit

explanation.surface: Mum gives the main help when she comes to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief prop or support, originally a stay holding up a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Fish and meat found by bird in sea

parts.note: ham is cured pork

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Fish, meat and a bird are all found at sea, like a mixed menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a shark with a flattened, hammer-shaped head, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Rude young offender vandalised toilet largely

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are disordered
largely means for the most part, so the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A youthful delinquent rudely trashed most of a public loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young offender' suggests a criminal; a mischievous imp is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite means lacking good manners, a direct synonym for rude.

clue.text: A qualification needed when encapsulating heartless individual, parasitic type

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the degree wraps round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a Master of Business Administration degree

indicators.note: without a heart the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A business degree enclosing a heartless person yields a parasite of a type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual' is the number one rather than a person; the heart removed is its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Some amoebas live as parasites, such as the one causing amoebic dysentery, so it names a kind of parasitic organism.

clue.text: Musical fixture excited short MEP

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small Euro-politician gets worked up about a concert season.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms is the BBC's annual summer series of classical concerts at the Royal Albert Hall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proms is a regular annual event in the classical calendar, a fixture in the scheduling sense.

clue.text: Guards in Spanish city getting corrective punishment

indicators.note: in places the guards inside the city name

parts.note: León is a city in northern Spain
the SS was the Nazi guard corps

explanation.surface: Guards stationed in a Spanish city hand out a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach someone a lesson is to punish them so they behave better, a sense of reprimand.

clue.text: Student in predicament almost restricted by unwelcome mark

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so it sits within the other piece

parts.note: a scar is an unwanted mark on the skin

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: being in a hole is being in difficulty

explanation.surface: A student is in a fix, constrained by a poor mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwelcome mark' suggests a bad grade; it is a blemish on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: African capital reportedly a graveyard for drivers?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: a final resting place for motor vehicles

explanation.surface: A city in Africa is said to be where motorists go to die.
explanation.walkthrough: Khartoum, capital of Sudan, is pronounced much like 'car tomb' in a British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Khartoum is the capital city of Sudan, at the meeting of the Blue and White Nile.

clue.text: How one might characterise pedestrian noise initially put out by a traditional music-maker

indicators.note: put out means thrown away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a pedestrian has no car, as in 'not in a car'

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A walker's noise is drowned out by an old instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A walker is someone with 'no car in a' journey; dropping the N leaves the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is an ancient egg-shaped vessel flute, a folk wind instrument.

clue.text: Covering shift in hours over day

indicators.note: a shift is a change of place, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone provides cover on a shift lasting hours across the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering shift' reads as a stand-in's work shift; the noun is the definition and the verb the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shroud is a cloth wrapped around a body, or anything that conceals, so a covering.

clue.text: Constant music around school and fast food outlet

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant such as the speed of light

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the music style encloses the school letter

parts.note: hip hop is a music genre
standard abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Music blares nonstop around a school and a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A chip shop is a British takeaway selling fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip shop serves fried fish and chips over the counter, an example of a fast food outlet.

clue.text: One wearing disgusted expression returning for part of flight

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the expression is read backwards
the one wearing something has it around them, so the expression encloses the one

parts.note: Rats! is an exclamation of annoyance
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face of disgust on the way back for part of a plane trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step, and a flight is a series of steps between floors.

clue.text: Deep sea fish

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a spiny-finned food fish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'deep-sea fish'; split it into a low voice and a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass describes the lowest range of voices or instruments; it is also a common sea perch.

clue.text: Large loo after one round is sunk drunk quickly found in bars?

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and staggering, so the letters reel into a new order
something sunk goes out of sight, so that letter vanishes

parts.note: taken as written
a single round letter O

explanation.surface: A drunk heads quickly for a big lavatory after one more round in the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The bars are bars of music, not pubs, and 'drunk' is the signal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a tempo marking for a brisk pace, so it describes music played fast within its bars.

clue.text: Published policy in preliminary plan

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
the party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A party sets out its policy in an early draft.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough sketch or summary giving the main features, a draft scheme.

clue.text: On reflection, what might be contained by cups, not singular container

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards
without the singular means the letter for singular is taken away

parts.words: what might be contained by cups
parts.note: the cups of a bra hold the bust
standard abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, someone ponders what fits in cups and a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: BUST loses its S to give BUT, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a wide open vessel for holding liquids or food, a kind of container.

clue.text: Arrangement not completed by very large investor

indicators.note: something not completed lacks its ending, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to sort is to arrange; a sort is an arrangement
OS is the clothing size outsize

explanation.surface: An unfinished deal is struck by a hugely wealthy financier.
explanation.walkthrough: George Soros is a famous billionaire hedge-fund investor.
explanation.definitionFit: George Soros made a fortune speculating on currencies, the best-known investor of that name.

clue.text: Part of estate, maybe, to frustrate group of executives

parts.note: to dash hopes is to frustrate them
a company's board of directors

explanation.surface: Part of a landed property is used to thwart a company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests land; it is an estate car, the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashboard is the instrument panel of a car, so it is part of any car, an estate being one example.
